item.title: Witness says pilot in Amazon crash was shaking afterward: "My career is over"
item.description: Abraham Altamar was on the phone with his wife when he briefly spoke with one of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that overran a runway in Miami.

item.title: Price of crude oil nears $100 a barrel as U.S.-Iran stalemate continues
item.description: Oil prices are rising steadily with no end in sight to the U.S.-Iran standoff impeding tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Floods surge in Hawaii as Hurricane Lowell roars
item.description: Floods are surging in the aftermath of Hurricane Lowell, which skirted the western side of Hawaii early Tuesday. CBS News' Carter Evans has the latest.

item.title: Names of victims in deadly Amazon cargo plane crash at MIA released
item.description: The Amazon cargo plane crashed off the end of a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, leaving five people dead and five others injured.

item.title: Lonnie Bunch, Smithsonian leader, to retire amid Trump criticism
item.description: Historian Lonnie Bunch will leave his position as secretary of the Smithsonian at the end of the year, he announced Tuesday.

item.title: Trump marks 25 years since 9/11 at "Steel Across America" event: "We will never forget"
item.description: President Trump marked 25 years since 9/11 at a "Steel Across America" event in Washington, D.C. Mr. Trump also talked about Iran, saying it would "never have a nuclear weapon."

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: It's time: 60 Minutes returns for season 59 on September 13
item.description: The 59th season premiere of 60 MINUTES airs Sunday, September 13, at 7:30 PM, ET/PT, after NFL football, on the CBS Television Network and streaming on Paramount+.

item.title: Patrick Clancy's lawyer threatens conspiracy theorists with legal action
item.description: Patrick Clancy, Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband, issued a scathing statement to conspiracy theorists who have been claiming he was involved in the deaths of the couple's children - "There will be consequences."

item.title: 4 found dead after Miami family's small plane goes missing off Bahamas
item.description: A small plane carrying four family members flying back home to Florida went missing off the Bahamas, the U.S. Coast Guard and authorities in the Bahamas said.

item.title: Trump's power to change mail voting is limited, election law expert says
item.description: President Trump appealed to the Supreme Court again in his legal fight to limit mail-in ballots. Election law expert David Becker joins to discuss.

item.title: Dangerous Hurricane Lowell passing just west of Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lowell was skirting western Hawaii, bringing damaging winds, heavy rain and punishing waves, the National Hurricane Center said.

item.title: Ohio gubernatorial hopeful Amy Acton thanks first responders after attempted attack
item.description: Amy Acton, Ohio's Democratic candidate for governor, thanked first responders after a man attempted to attack her. Several others were injured in the attack. CBS News' Ash-har Quraishi reports.

item.title: 9/11 survivors and responders grapple with physical and mental health 25 years later
item.description: Survivors and first responders still struggle with physical ailments and poor mental health, 25 years after the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks.

item.title: London police use tech to tackle masked phone snatchers
item.description: Police say fewer people in London are getting their phones stolen by criminals speeding by on bikes and mopeds thanks to a dedicated task force with an "eye in the sky."

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan will not be working royals, King Charles says
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are back in the United Kingdom, but King Charles says that the couple will not be working royals. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry has more.

item.title: Drought causes Panama Canal traffic jam
item.description: There's a slowdown at the Panama Canal due to low water levels. CBS News' Lilia Luciano explains more.

item.title: U.S. envoy warns U.K. against new plan to sanction Israeli settlements
item.description: Britain and 11 other U.S. allies say they'll sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, citing an "unprecedented level of settler violence."

item.title: Latest in Trump's fight to limit mail voting
item.description: The Trump administration is again requesting that the Supreme Court weigh in on mail-in voting restrictions. Election law expert David Becker explains where things stand in the legal fight.

item.title: Goldman Sachs warns oil prices could hit $120 as U.S. fuel costs surge
item.description: Higher gas and diesel prices have cost Americans an additional $100 billion since the Iran war began, according to a Brown University tracker.

item.title: Oil prices near $100 a barrel as Houthis launch new attacks on Saudi energy points
item.description: Oil prices are spiking again as tensions rise in the Middle East and the war in Iran rages on. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady has more.

item.title: Republicans gather in Texas for party's first-ever midterm convention
item.description: Prominent Republicans are headed to their first-ever midterm convention. CBS News' Shawna Mizelle reports.

item.title: Patrick Clancy's lawyer threatens legal action against conspiracy theorists
item.description: Patrick Clancy's lawyer threatened legal action against those who claim he had a role in his children's death. The statement came after a Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in his ex-wife Lindsay Clancy's murder trial. Shanelle Kaul has the latest.

item.title: John Legend says his new album is "transporting" and "cinematic"
item.description: John Legend announced a new album, "Muse," set to be released in late October. Legend sat down with Nate Burleson to discuss the album's new sound and his collaboration with Pharrell.

item.title: Alexandra Eala on what she hopes fellow Filipinos take away from her U.S. Open appearance
item.description: Filipino tennis star Alexandra Eala, who achieved a career-best run at a Grand Slam tournament after reaching the third round of the U.S. Open and losing to Iva Jovic, joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss her performance and how her tennis career began.

item.title: Data center development turns some landowners into millionaires
item.description: Most Americans say they're opposed to data centers. But a lucky few have gotten rich selling their land to data center developers.

item.title: Canada matches Trump's steep U.S. tariffs in ongoing trade war
item.description: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on various U.S. goods have arrived. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Jill Is Rooting for a Crash?! | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: You read that right: Jill is rooting for a market crash. In today's episode, Certified Financial Planner Kayla Sabbagh joins Jill and Mark to explain why Jill might be onto something—and how, in some cases, a market crash can be good for your wallet. Plus, Jill and the gang help caller Jessica make a financial plan for her move across the country.

item.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods take effect
item.description: Canada's steep retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. goods took effect just after midnight ET on Tuesday, deepening the trade war between the two countries.

item.title: King says Prince Harry and Meghan remain private citizens after U.K. return
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan stepped down as senior working members of the royal family in January 2020, and this position, the letter said, "will continue to be fully respected."
